speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you describe the appearance of the rash in more detail, such as whether it is raised, flat, or blistered, and when exactly it started?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text: The rash typically starts on the face and spreads to the trunk and limbs, often described as looking like "slapped cheeks" followed by a lacy rash. Does the rash on her body have a lacy or reticular pattern, and does it seem to worsen when she is in the sun or after a hot bath?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Mildly pruritic rash on trunk and extremities. I also have Low-grade fever, Rhinorrhea, Headache, Facial rash not involving the perioral skin.

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of a facial rash sparing the mouth area followed by a lacy body rash, along with mild systemic symptoms, is highly characteristic of Erythema Infectiosum, also known as Fifth Disease. DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease)
